3G.13 It is good and pleasant for brethren to dwell together in unity.
Skirt
Unity

precepts.text: How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight? Unity. Through us together, unified in Christ, hence the name Israel United in Christ, we can move mountains. Some others do not aspire to do anything; they are fine doing videos from their garages. But the vision here has been set at a worldwide standard. If you do not have worldwide aspirations, you are not going to do worldwide things; if you think small, you will stay small.
precepts.point: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity. Why is that good and pleasant? Because we cannot be stopped when we are unified.
precepts.why:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Why is that good and pleasant? It's the only way we grow, keeping the commandments together as a unit; without unity there is disorder, and nothing gets built. But the reason it is so important is that we can't be stopped when we are unified. Moses shows it: “How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight”?

Unity. That's how we are going to do it: through us together, unified in Christ. Hence the name Israel United in Christ. We can move mountains. It's that type of unity we have to come to and understand, because without it, brothers, we won't do nothing.

Look at some of the others, not doing anything. They don't aspire to do anything; they're fine just where they're at, cool just being in the house, and they will keep doing videos from their garages. But we have worldwide goals. The vision here has been set at a worldwide standard. If you don't have worldwide aspirations, you're not going to do worldwide things. If you think small, you'll stay small. Shoot for the stars.

The sixty-man camp of 2013 showed it: that small number organized and unified set a standard in the nation, and today one phone call could bring a thousand men. That is one chasing a thousand and two putting ten thousand to flight, when brethren dwell together in unity.

precepts.text: In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, and a man and a wife that agree together. All three are unity in righteousness. It is not that oogly googly feeling about your neighbor; it is unity in righteousness. A sanctified holy marriage that has come together in the Lord is a beautiful thing before the Lord. Anything other than that is not beautiful; the Lord is not beautified. Remember how Paul wrote to the different schools: you are puffed up, there are all types of schisms among you. That is not unity. To be unified means to come together in holiness and righteousness the way God meant it to be.
precepts.point: If you are spiritual, you understand this unity is not talking about gang banging, not the fraternities, not Freemasonry, none of that worldly foolishness some of us came out of. This unification is talking about being unified in Christ. Hence the name Israel United in Christ. To be united in the Lord is true unity.
precepts.why:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Some think this is just talking about a bunch of Negroes coming together, a bunch of brothers together, and that's beautiful. No, it is much more than that. If you are spiritual, you understand this unity is not gang banging, not the Hoovers, not the Omegas, Kappas and Alphas, not Freemasonry, none of that worldly nonsense some of us came out of. It is being unified in Christ; hence the name Israel United in Christ.

Sirach shows what unity God is beautified by: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

The unity of brethren in what? In righteousness. The love of neighbours is not that oogly googly feeling, that's my neighbor, we're good friends; it is unity in righteousness, someone that shows care for their nation and their people. A man and a wife that agree together, in righteousness: a sanctified holy marriage that has come together in the Lord is a beautiful thing before the Lord.

Anything other than that is not beautiful, and the Lord is not beautified by it. Remember how Paul wrote to the different schools: you are puffed up, there are all types of schisms among you. That is not unity. To be unified means to come together in holiness and righteousness, the way God meant it to be and the way Christ told us to be. And that unification of the nation of Israel is the highest known threat to this evil world; it scares them.

precepts.text: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity; the feasts gather the nation.
precepts.point: Pharaoh offered to let only the men go, and Moses and Aaron were driven out from his presence.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
Pharaoh asked who would go, and Moses answered, “We will go with our young and with our old, with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds will we go; for we must hold a feast unto the Lord.” Not the men only, as Pharaoh offered: everyone, young and old, sons and daughters, flocks and herds.

“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” The Most High loves to see Israel gathered together in unity. That is why so many feast days bring the nation together to honour him: a feast unto the Lord is the whole nation, and Moses would not hold one with half of it left in Egypt. Pharaoh said “go now ye that are men”, and Moses and Aaron were driven out from his presence.

precepts.text: Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity; the brotherhood that keeps the oil in your life.
precepts.point: Though Israel is in captivity now without a temple, without lamps to bring oil for, and no longer under the Levitical priesthood, think about it spiritually: you have to keep your lamp lit and keep the oil in your life. Brotherhood and unity, and correction, which is an excellent oil that shall not break the head, are that oil; if you are not around a body being built up and corrected by teachers and peers, that is how people run out of oil, their lamp goes out, and they fall out of this truth and do not endure to the end. The ten virgins with their lamps and oil come to mind here, offered as a meditation.

note.label: Exodus 27: The Altar, the Court, and the Oil for the Lamp

precepts.why:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!”

Brotherhood and unity are the oil that keeps your lamp burning. If you are not around a body being built up, that is how people run out of oil: their lamp goes out, and they fall out of this truth and do not endure to the end. The ten virgins with their lamps and oil come to mind here, as a meditation.

precepts.text: Unity among brethren is like the precious ointment upon Aaron's head that ran down his beard to the skirts of his garments; for there the LORD commanded the blessing.
precepts.point: This is what David is going back to in the psalm: behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity; it is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron's beard, down to the skirts of his garments. That oil could be poured on no one but the high priest; that is how precious unity among the people is to be.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
Moses poured of the anointing oil upon Aaron’s head and anointed him, to sanctify him, to set him apart. That is what David is going back to: “Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity! It is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron’s beard: that went down to the skirts of his garments”.

That oil could be poured on no one but the high priest; that is how precious unity among the people is to be. It is like the dew too: “As the dew of Hermon, and as the dew that descended upon the mountains of Zion: for there the Lord commanded the blessing, even life for evermore.”

precepts.text: James to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, my brethren.
precepts.point: It is good for us to dwell among ourselves because that is all we have; everybody else hates our guts, a thing we understand as we grow in the truth. We admonish, edify, comfort, and esteem one another in the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 133: The Brethren Dwelling Together in Unity

precepts.why: “Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” The brethren are the twelve tribes scattered abroad worldwide: James writes “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. It is good for us to dwell among ourselves because that is all we have; everybody else hates our guts, a thing we understand as we grow in the truth.

precepts.text: Comfort and edify one another, know them which labor among you and are over you in the Most High, and esteem them highly in love.
precepts.point: It is good for us to dwell among ourselves because that is all we have; everybody else hates our guts, a thing we understand as we grow in the truth. We admonish, edify, comfort, and esteem one another in the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 133: The Brethren Dwelling Together in Unity

precepts.why:
Dwelling together in unity looks like this: “comfort yourselves together, and edify one another”, “know them which labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you; And to esteem them very highly in love for their work’s sake. And be at peace among yourselves.” Then “warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men.”

We admonish, edify, comfort, and esteem one another in the scriptures. That is how good and how pleasant it is for the brethren, the twelve tribes, to dwell together, because everybody else hates our guts and we are all we have.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

precepts.why:
“That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee”. Christ is praying that we may be one with him. “that they also may be one in us”. That's unity. Come together, one mind, one spirit, one body. That's the unity we teach in IUIC.

“that they may be one, even as we are one”. Christ gives them the glory the Father gave him. “I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one”. Perfect in one. That's unity.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

precepts.why:
“A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another”. Christ gives us the commandment to love each other. That's unity. “as I have loved you”. The same way he loves you, he wants you to love one another. “By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples”. How will they know you're his disciple? “if ye have love one to another.” By loving each other.

If you don't show love to another brother, you're not Christ's disciple. You're Satan's disciple. Everybody running their mouth showing hatred is Satan's disciple, not Christ's. Loving each other is how people tell the difference.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

precepts.why: “For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office”. We're different members. “So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.” That's unity. Many members, but one in Christ.
